documents.title: Database Fundamentals
documents.content: A database is an organized collection of structured data that is stored and accessed electronically. Databases use a database management system (DBMS) to manage data efficiently. The most common type is a relational database, which organizes data into tables with rows and columns. SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to query and manipulate data in relational databases. Indexes are data structures that improve the speed of data retrieval operations on a table.

documents.title: Query Optimization
documents.content: Query optimization is the process of choosing the most efficient means of processing a SQL statement. The query optimizer is a component of the database management system that determines the most efficient way to execute a query. Execution plans are generated by the query optimizer to outline how the database will execute a query. Statistics and cost estimation help the optimizer choose between different execution strategies. Query performance depends on proper index selection and table design.

documents.title: Data Integrity and Constraints
documents.content: Data integrity refers to the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of data throughout its lifecycle. Database constraints are rules that enforce data quality and consistency. Primary keys uniquely identify each row in a table. Foreign keys establish relationships between tables and maintain referential integrity. Unique constraints prevent duplicate values in columns. Check constraints validate that column values meet specific conditions. Constraints are essential for maintaining the consistency and reliability of data in databases.
